text:
A farmer had three sons. They always argued and fought. The farmer was sad.

One day, he called his sons. “Bring me some sticks,” he said.

The sons brought many sticks. The farmer tied them together in a bundle.

“Now,” he said to the oldest son, “break this bundle.”

The son tried with all his strength, but he could not break it. The second son tried. He also failed. The youngest son tried too, but it was impossible.

Then the farmer opened the bundle. He gave each son one stick. “Now break them,” he said.

Each son broke his stick easily. Snap! Snap! Snap!

“Do you see?” said the farmer. “One stick is weak. But many sticks together are strong. If you stand together, no one can hurt you. If you fight, anyone can break you.”

The sons looked at each other. They felt ashamed. From that day on, they helped each other and lived in peace.

Moral: We are stronger together.

quiz.q: The oldest son broke the bundle of sticks.
What did the farmer want to teach his sons?
What happened when each son had one stick?
o: Each one broke his stick easily
